title: Measurement for Dummies? Exploring the Role of Regulatory Metrics and Firm Strategy
eligible_reason: Binary treatment 'major' (= 1 for vehicle model years at or after the model's first major redesign following the 1994 side-impact-dummy regulation) switches on at model-specific model years (9 in-sample adoption cohorts, 1995-2003) with never-treated models; Table 2 Panel A Column 1 is a static linear regression of occupant fatality on major with vehicle-model (mmid) and model-year (modelyr) fixed effects and no controls.
design_notes: Observation = occupant in a crash (repeated cross-section, 29,917 rows, accident years 1991-2007), assigned to vehicle model (mmid, 543 models) x model year (modelyr, 1975-2003) cells. Treatment major = 1 iff modelyr >= post94, where post94 is the model year of the vehicle model's first major redesign after 1994 (mmid-specific; missing for 6,553 rows = models with no post-1994 redesign). Verified in maindata.dta: major==1 exactly when modelyr>=post94 (0 exceptions), never switches off. Among 543 mmids: 320 never treated in sample, 136 switch within sample, 87 observed only in treated model years (always-treated). In-sample first-treated model years: 1995 (47 models), 1996 (14), 1997 (30), 1998 (24), 1999 (30), 2000 (27), 2001 (18), 2002 (17), 2003 (16). The 'calendar time' dimension is vehicle model year; accident year (year) varies within cells and enters other columns as i.year fixed effects plus crash/occupant covariates (time-varying at the observation level), which makes Columns 2-5 ineligible. Panel B interacts major with the SID-like-occupant indicator (subgroup-by-treatment interaction, ineligible). Tables 3-5 split the sample by firm type (odi_safe, patent_metric) but all include the covariates and i.year (ineligible). Figure 2 is an event study (i.yr_to_sidcar) with covariates and i.year, with never-treated and <-5 bins pooled (ineligible). Full-text flags indicate the paper discusses Goodman-Bacon, Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham and Borusyak et al., but the replication code implements only reghdfe TWFE.

specs.code: eststo base: reghdfe fatal major, absorb(modelyr mmid) vce(cluster make)
specs.outcome_description: occupant fatality indicator (0/1); linear probability model
specs.treatment_definition: 1 if modelyr >= post94, where post94 = model year of the vehicle model's first major redesign after 1994 (missing = never redesigned in sample)
specs.sample_condition: all rows of maindata.dta (29,917; reghdfe drops 79 singletons -> 29,838)
specs.notes: Repeated cross-section of crash occupants assigned to mmid x modelyr cells; time dimension is vehicle model year, not accident year. 87 always-treated models and 320 never-treated models are present.

ineligible_main_text_specs.reason: observation-level time-varying covariates (crash, occupant, vehicle age) and accident-year FE i.year
major##sid subgroup-by-treatment interaction (Column 1 without covariates still has the interaction)
subsample splits by firm type with covariates, i.year and major##sid interactions
event study with covariates and i.year; never-treated pooled into the <-5 bin

preferred_spec_note: Column 1 is the no-controls baseline; the author's preferred estimate is probably Column 4 (full covariates), which is ineligible. Column 1 coefficient (-0.0165) is nearly identical to the other columns.
data_files: mnsc_data/maindata.dta (29,917 x 27; variables year, modelyr, make, mmid, post94, major, sid, fatal, covariates, parent_company, odi_safe, patent_metric)
software_detail: Stata 18, reghdfe; log file maindata.log and .tex table outputs included
screener_notes: No article text available; screened from code, README, log and abstract. For CSA: repeated cross-section (panel=FALSE) with idname = mmid, tname = modelyr, gname = post94 (recode missing to 0 for never-treated; cohorts after 2003 are never treated in sample), cluster = make; for BJS imputation treat mmid x modelyr as the unit-period cell. Note that make has only 47 clusters and the always-treated models (87) contribute no identifying variation under CSA. The paper's full-text flags for Borusyak/Callaway/Sun-Abraham come from the text, not from the code.
